verified_round1.url_checked: https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.15627 (full v1 text read twice with the alphaXiv tools); https://casrai.org/news/autosupercon-llm-extraction-superconducting-parameters-2026 (secondary editorial); Hugging Face dataset search for 'autosupercon' (no hits); web search for GitHub, Zenodo or Figshare (no hits); NEMAD paper arXiv:2512.10847 read to compare corpora
verified_round1.access_verified: [Certain] v1 is stamped 11 Nov 2026 [cond-mat.supr-con]. The full text has no data-availability section and no repository or URL for the database. The CASRAI editorial (published 15 Nov, updated 25 Nov 2026) gives no download link either. [Certain] No Hugging Face dataset and no web hit for a repository. [Likely] Not public as of 27 Nov 2026; the only route is a request to the corresponding authors listed on the paper.
verified_round1.license_verified: unknown: no licence or data statement in v1 [Certain]
verified_round1.size_verified: 20,354 entries for 6,793 superconductors; 5,843 bulk ambient-pressure Tc materials; 2,439 matched NIMS [Certain, from the paper]
verified_round1.label_quality: [Certain] Labels were extracted by gpt-5-mini (2025-08-07 snapshot) in strict structured-output mode, from text segments that contained a parameter keyword, a number with a unit and 'superconduct'. Preprints are not peer-reviewed. Cleaning used pymatgen formula standardisation, rejected unresolved variables, applied per-parameter range filters, took medians over duplicates and applied cross-parameter inequality filters. Validation against NIMS on 2,439 shared superconductors gave R2 = 0.96 overall, R2 = 0.83 for Tc <= 30 K and a median deviation of 0.25 K (3.5%). The worst outliers came from known failure modes: photoinduced transient Tc read as equilibrium, and theoretical values read as measured. Roberts Table 5 was transcribed by Gemini 3 Flash: 605 rows became 404 materials, contributing 639 entries and 254 new superconductors. [Likely] It contains positives only; no negative or 'not superconducting' records are described.
verified_round1.why: [Certain] Size: 20,354 entries, 6,793 superconductors, 84 elements, 8 parameters. 75% of entries are at ambient pressure and 25% under pressure. The bulk ambient-pressure Tc subset has 5,843 materials, and 1,204 materials have Hc2. The corpus is more than 47,000 arXiv cond-mat.supr-con preprints posted up to March 2026. [Certain] NEMAD, which the project already holds, was built from about 90,000 APS and Elsevier DOIs (publisher XML) plus handbooks, not from arXiv, and it records about 14,000 compositions not in SuperCon. [Likely] Most cond-mat.supr-con preprints are published in APS or Elsevier journals, so overlap with NEMAD and SuperCon2 should be large. Genuine novelty would be 2021-2026 compositions and the Hc2, penetration-depth and gap parameters. [Speculative] Perhaps 1,000-2,000 new compositions, all positives. At the project's learning curve (+0.03 AUC per doubling), that is under +0.01 AUC, and positives alone do not add hard negatives near the project's own rows. For the room-temperature goal, the superfluid-density ceiling (Tc proportional to 1/lambda0^2) and the gap data could feed physics screening features, but the data contains no new high-Tc ambient-pressure mater
verified_round1.next_step: Ask the corresponding authors on arXiv:2611.15627 for the database and its licence, through the owner and not from an automated account. Watch for a v2 with a data link. When it is available, standardise formulas the same way as the cycle-7 table and count compositions absent from SuperCon2, NEMAD and NIMS, split by pre- and post-2021. Use the new positives and the pressure and sample-form fields to correct high-pressure mislabels. Do not expect AUC gains above about 0.01.

verified_round1.label_quality: [Certain] Entries are manually extracted by the PAULING FILE team from peer-reviewed papers and tied to a specific phase (formula, space group, Pearson symbol) and to a source paper. Example journals in the results: Phys Rev B 1973, phys. stat. sol. (a) 1977/1993/1994, Solid State Commun 1964-1990, J Less-Common Met 1976-1990, J Alloys Compd 1996-2001, JMMM 1988-1992, J Phys Cond Matter 1995/2015, JPSJ/JJAP 2015. The property group covers Tc, 'lowest temperature of investigation', composition and pressure derivatives, 'superconductivity' and 'critical pressure for superconductivity'. A single phase often has several entries, e.g. BaPt2As2 has 9. I could not assess error rates. The phase resolution is a real advantage over SuperCon [Likely].
verified_round1.why: [Certain] estimated_count values: 27,734 for the superconductivity property group, 3,046 for 'lowest temperature of investigation' alone, and 2,731 for 2015-2026. These count entries, not distinct materials; given repeated entries per phase, distinct phases are probably well under 27.7K [Speculative]. The journal set (Phys Rev B, Solid State Commun, J Less-Common Met, J Alloys Compd, JPSJ, J Phys Cond Matter) overlaps the NIMS refno journal codes heavily. The project's cycle-7 table already contains about 1,955 of the NIMS non-cuprate negatives. So the compositions behind the 3,046 negative entries are probably largely duplicates [Likely]. The likely new value is phase-resolved labels for polymorph conflicts, links to experimental structures, and an independent second reading for the label-noise audit, not many new compositions. Post-2015 coverage (2,731 entries) is small next to SuperCon2 (to 2021) and NEMAD (to 2025). Cost and licence restrictions keep the value low unless an institutional subscription exists.
verified_round1.next_step: Ask the owner to check whether their university library subscribes to ASM MPDS. If it does, pull the 'lowest temperature of investigation' and Tc entries through the API with an institutional key, map phases to compositions, and measure overlap with the cycle-7 table before deciding on any import. Use the entries mainly to settle the 265 NIMS positive-versus-tcn conflicts by phase. Do not bulk-scrape the free search endpoint without MPDS permission. Low priority compared with importing the remaining clean NIMS tcn rows and auditing those conflicts.

Tn values and reference numbers are mostly readable, but formula subscripts land on separate lines and some rows lose their material name, so formulas need layout-aware reassembly or a multimodal-LLM transcription. verified_round1.license_verified: [Certain] p. 581 reads: 'Copyright (c) 1976 by the U.S. Secretary of Commerce on behalf of the United States. This copyright will be assigned to the American Institute of Physics and the American Chemical Society, to whom all requests regarding reproduction should be addressed.' The reprint header reads '(c) 1976 American Institute of Physics for the National Institute of Standards and Technology.' Reuse and redistribution terms are unclear. Using the numeric facts internally is probably low risk [Speculative; not legal advice].
verified_round1.size_verified: [Likely; my own counts from the text layer] Table 2 has about 4,300-4,700 reference-bearing lines (about 33 per page over about 140 pages). Tables 2-4 have about 1,085-1,120 rows with a Tn value (two independent parsers agree). About 50 rows give Tc as an upper bound ('<x') in the Tc column. The bibliography runs to reference [1994]. This matches the estimate of 1-3K Tn rows at the low end.
verified_round1.label_quality: [Certain] p. 585: Tables 2-4 'contain data on negative experiments in the column headed Tn, which is the temperature in K down to which the material has been checked specifically for a superconductive transition without success'. Ferri-, antiferro- and ferromagnets were excluded. Values are quoted as the authors gave them; P marks pressure in kbar; there are many dilute-alloy Tc-shift, thin-film, implanted and quench-condensed rows. The negatives are censored and often shallow: very common values are 1.02 or 1.28 K (refs 270, 011, 084), which only exclude Tc above about 1 K. Corrections to the brief: (1) Al2Pt '0.55-0.48' sits in the Tc column (C1, refs 486, 037), so it is a superconductor, not a Tn example; the Tn entry nearby is AlPt (CUB) at 0.34 K. (2) Al2Zr '<0.35' is a Tc upper bound in the Tc column, not a Tn entry. The project's NIMS file has Al2Zr1 with Tc mid = recommended = 0.35 (ref RMP0350001), which looks like an upper bound turned into a positive label. About 50 such '<x' rows exist and are worth auditing. Ag5Ba (D2d, 0.34 K, ref 486) and AgMg (B2, 1.02 K) are confirmed Tn entries.
verified_round1.why: [Likely, measured] I parsed 1,085 (Tn, Roberts reference number) pairs and matched them against the project's own NIMS file, data/raw/nims-supercon/20240322_MDR_OAndM.txt, using column 81 'lowest temperature for measurement (not superconducting)' (4,641 filled rows; about 1,340 with publication year before 1975). 863 pairs (80%) match exactly on both Tn and the integer reference number, and 88% of the reference numbers appear in NIMS. Spot checks of unmatched rows found them filed under journal codes instead; Roberts ref 270 is NIMS 'RMP0350001', for example MnRe 1.02 and NbZn3 1.02. 11 of 12 named examples are present with the same Tn and reference (Ag5Ba, AgMg, AgBe2, AgBi, CeNi2, Al2Lu, B2Th, RuSe2, PbV3, ...). So the bulk route to these negatives is NIMS column 81, which the project holds but has not imported. Every row is a low-Tc conventional material from before 1975, so it adds nothing to the room-temperature goal.
verified_round1.next_step: Import NIMS column 81 (tcn) as censored negatives carrying the threshold temperature, and treat Tn of 1.5 K or below as weak negatives. Use the Roberts PDF only to audit what is left: about 200 unmatched Tn rows and about 50 '<x' Tc-column rows that NIMS may have turned into positives, such as Al2Zr. Do not OCR all 140 pages.

verified_round1.url_checked: https://nvlpubs.nist.gov/nistpubs/Legacy/TN/nbstechnicalnote983.pdf (DOI 10.6028/NBS.TN.983). I fetched it with WebFetch: 104 PDF pages, 4.6 MB, an Internet Archive scan. verified_round1.access_verified: [Certain] Free PDF. The title page reads 'Issued October 1978', 'Nat. Bur. Stand. (U.S.), Tech. Note 983, 99 pages (October 1978)'; the scan also carries an 'OCT 18 1979' library stamp. It 'extends' the 1976 survey and 'supersedes NBS Technical Note 825'. The abstract covers 'world literature up to fall 1977' and 'the results of negative experiments'. Contents: Table 2 runs from p. 14 to p. 54 (Table 3 starts at p. 55), so about 41 pages rather than about 35. The OCR text layer is badly garbled for formulas (for example ''^90.82'^^ 0.18'); Tn values and reference numbers are readable, so formulas need manual or multimodal-LLM transcription.
verified_round1.license_verified: [Certain] The author was not an NBS employee: B. W. Roberts, Superconductive Materials Data Center, General Electric Corporate Research and Development, Schenectady. The work was 'partially supported by the NBS Office of Standard Reference Data', and the report documentation page has a Contract/Grant field. I found no copyright notice in the text layer. Public-domain status as a US Government work is therefore unclear, not 'likely' [Speculative].
verified_round1.size_verified: [Likely; my own counts] Table 2 has about 990 reference-bearing rows (about 25 per page over 40 pages), at the low end of the 1-2K estimate. Only about 56-65 rows carry a Tn value, so it holds far fewer negatives than its size suggests. [Certain] Its new references are numbered 1996-2411, with a few older numbers (1266, 1810) listed again; the 1976 survey's bibliography ends at about [1994].
verified_round1.label_quality: [Certain] Same Tn definition: 'Tables 2-3 contain data on negative experiments in the column headed Tn ... checked specifically for a superconductive transition without success'; materials found to be only ferri-, antiferro- or ferromagnetic are excluded. Many rows are implanted, amorphous, quench-condensed, liquid-quenched or thin-film samples, or Chevrel phases (for example AgMo6S8, 8.9 K). Correction to the brief: AuLu is not a 0.04 K negative. TN 983 lists AuLu with Tc 0.37 K (ref 2006). The 0.04 K B2 or Heusler negatives from ref 2006 (Matthias, Corenzwit, Vandenberg, Barz, Maple, Shelton) are AgLu, AgSc, AgY, AuY, CuLu, CuSc, Au2GaLa, Au2GaSc, Au2GaY and Au2InLa. These are deep negatives (tested to 0.04 K) and therefore strong ones.
verified_round1.why: [Likely, measured against the project's NIMS file] The NIMS datasheet's largest integer reference number is 1995, so TN 983's references (1996-2411) were not imported by number, and none of the 56 parsed (Tn, refno) pairs match. Some of its papers do appear under journal codes. NIMS cites LES0460339 (J. Less-Common Met. 46, 339 (1976), which is TN 983 ref 2006) for 6 positives (CuY 0.47, AuSc 2, AuLu 0.37, Au2AlSc 4.4, Au2InSc 3.02, Au2InY 1.9) but for none of the ten 0.04 K negatives from the same paper. Of 16 TN 983 negatives I checked by formula, 15 have no NIMS tcn row at that Tn; only BNb (1.1 K, NIMS ref MRB0100889) is present. Of 39 cleanly parsed positive formulas, 30 already have NIMS rows; about 9 compositions look absent (for example PtTi, STh, P3Rh4, PTa3, IrZr, AsGeTe), though OCR parse errors are possible. The genuinely new yield is about 50-60 negatives plus perhaps 100-250 positive rows. That is far too few to move AUC, given about +0.03 per doubling of thousands of compositions. They are all low-Tc materials from the 1970s.
verified_round1.next_step: Optional, cheap: transcribe the roughly 60 Tn rows by hand or with a vision LLM (an afternoon's work) and add them as censored negatives tagged 'NBS TN 983'. Then diff the clean positive formulas against NIMS. Do not expect an AUC gain; treat it as a small hard-negative set for B2 and Heusler intermetallics.

That matches the project's QE/Hazel toolchain and could save relax steps or provide cross-checks for Hazel candidates. It also gives a legal route to relaxed versions of ICSD- or MPDS-only polymorphs that Materials Project lacks (14,410 MPDS-unique structures). It largely missed four kinds: (1) measured nonmetal labels (Zhuo 2018 / Matbench, 4,921 compositions); (2) calculated Eliashberg sets beyond the held ones (Hennig group: BETE-NET 818 alpha2F under Apache-2.0; the BEE-NET screen with 741 DFT Tc>5 K plus 2 measured new superconductors; Geisler 2026, about 7,300 compounds with Eliashberg Tc and Hc2, not yet released); (3) pressure-resolved hydride sets (Tokuyama 2,059 records; Belli/Zurek 244 on figshare), which are irrelevant to the ambient goal; (4) bulk text routes for mining nulls (JARVIS arXiv abstracts, 1.8M; OpenAlex full text, 51,257 hits since 2015 for 'no superconductivity' AND 'down to').

HOW FAR THE DATA CAN GO (arithmetic [Certain]; applicability [Speculative]).
- At +0.03 AUC per doubling, moving from 0.80 to 0.90 needs about 3.3 doublings, or roughly 10 times the labelled compositions. No combination of the sources found adds that many non-duplicate measured compositions; the new ones total low thousands.
- Label noise caps measured AUC even for a perfect model. If 10% of labelled positives are really negative and 10% of labelled negatives are really positive, a perfect scorer's observed AUC is (0.9)(0.9) + 0.5(0.1)(0.9) + 0.5(0.1)(0.1) = 0.86.
- NEMAD shows about 10% label error. Unless the evaluation rows are cleaned, the 0.9 target may be unmeasurable rather than unreachable. Label cleaning of the test set, hard negatives near the project's rows, and calculated lambda/alpha2F as auxiliary targets are likely worth more than raw row counts.
